paragraphs.S66.C000.P000: On the fourth day, they stayed in Hveragerði. By noon, the rain had thickened, and Eric replaced the walk through the exposed stretch with a greenhouse café. Inside, it was hot, the glass had fogged, and lamps hung between the rows of tomatoes, making the faces seem slightly unreal. The tour ended with a practical activity: anyone who wanted could transplant seedlings for the school group arriving the next day.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P001: “At last, a place where my jacket isn't trying to kill me,” Nick said.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P002: He took it off and discovered that the T-shirt underneath was inside out. Alice noticed, but said nothing: Nick looked tired after the drive.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P003: A young employee explained how hot water from underground warmed the plants and bumblebees pollinated the tomatoes. Nick listened without his camera—the damp air was settling on the lens. Alice took off her coat first and asked to be shown how to remove a seedling without damaging its roots.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P004: “Are you nervous without it?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P005: “A little,” Nick admitted. “With it, at least I know where to put my hands.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P006: The employee handed them blank seedling tags. Alice placed one in his palm.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P008: He smiled and took the marker.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P009: The employee showed them a table with seedlings and tags. Eric carried the trays to an empty row, Nick labelled the varieties, Damir held the pots while Alice distributed the soil. When Nick mixed up two stacks of tags, the three of them sorted them by the sample, and Eric brought a new empty tray. For an hour, they stopped being people waiting for the next tourist stop: they had a small shared task.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P010: When the last tray was in place, the employee offered each of them a small tomato to taste. Nick reached first, but stopped and asked permission to take another. Passing Alice, Eric placed his own in her palm—she had not had time to take one from the tray.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P013: Damir examined the heating pipes. After difficult shifts, he used to become absorbed in the workings of anything that functioned without his help. Now he explained to Alice how he guessed the water moved beneath the rows and asked the employee to check his theory. He was wrong; Alice saw that it amused him more than it embarrassed him.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P014: Nick labelled the last tag and held out the marker to Alice. Soil still covered his fingers, and the camera was still in his bag. She held his wrist to read the variety name in his crooked handwriting. He did not joke, only asked quietly:
paragraphs.S66.C000.P017: She let go of his hand; he stood beside her for another second before returning to the table.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P018: They did not stay long in the café: they had something hot and returned to the seedling table to check that every tag was in the right place. One variety was missing. Nick had already reached for a name to invent, but Alice found the fallen order sheet under a tray.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P019: “Lucky,” he said, handing her the marker. “Will you write it? Your handwriting is clearer.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P020: “That's the first good reason to bring a journalist on a trip.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P021: Eric counted the finished pots with the employee. Damir carried the remaining soil back. Nick did not film: his hands were in the dirt, and Alice liked seeing him occupied without his usual excuse of the camera.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P022: When they left the greenhouse, the rain had nearly stopped. The employee opened a side door onto a short path beside a row of hot pipes. From there, they could see lamps glowing behind the glass and several more workers moving about. Alice suggested walking to the end of the path before returning to the car. Nick went first, Eric stayed by the door to make sure it did not slam shut, and Damir caught up with Alice carrying the scarf she had forgotten.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P023: “You left it on the back of the chair again,” he said.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P024: “At least the backpack is where it should be.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P025: Damir smiled. In their former life, he would have wrapped the scarf around her neck himself. Now he simply handed it to her.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P026: At the car, Alice discovered a streak of soil on her finger. Eric silently held out a wet wipe, then, catching her eye, said:
paragraphs.S66.C000.P027: “I took two. I don't want to look too prepared.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P028: She laughed and left the second one with him.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P029: On the way back, they argued about road music. Nick demanded that everyone choose a song they would be ashamed of. Eric admitted to loving an old pop group, but refused to name it. Damir chose a song Alice did not know. It hurt more than it should have: he had music in which she did not exist.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P030: And then he played the track, and she understood that it was beautiful.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P031: Outside the car window, wet roads, low houses, and a strip of brightening sky passed by. Nick tapped his fingers against his knee. Eric drove and quietly sang along with the chorus; when Alice turned toward him, he stopped. Damir looked out the window.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P032: Alice did not open her notebook.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P033: That evening, they returned to the guesthouse. Alice spread her notebook on the table and wrote the first lines for Marina—about how people with different histories had spent an hour doing one task without assigning roles in advance.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P034: Behind the wall, Nick searched for his charger and asked everyone not to move his bag; Damir found it under a chair. Eric checked tomorrow's departure time against the forecast. Alice put down her pen and went out onto the small terrace. The rain had stopped, but the railing was wet, and the air smelled of earth and smoke from the neighboring house. Through the kitchen glass, Nick and Damir argued about who should wash the thermoses. Eric stood in the hallway with a phone to his ear, speaking Icelandic—quickly, in a voice completely different from the measured one he used to explain plans to the group.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P035: He ended the call and noticed Alice.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P037: “An observation or an order to come back inside?”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P038: “An observation. An order would be longer.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P039: Eric stepped onto the terrace, leaving the door ajar.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P041: “The owner of the next house is warning us about road repairs. Nothing serious.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P042: “Do you always say ‘nothing serious’ with that expression?”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P044: “As if you've already thought of four backup routes and dislike the fifth.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P045: Eric braced his hands on the railing.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P048: “And I really don't like the fifth.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P052: “Eleven. I missed Nick dropping the spoon.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P056: She looked through the glass. Nick was proving something, waving a towel. Damir was laughing and holding both thermoses out of his reach.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P057: “It's strange,” Alice said. “When you don't write something down, it feels as if the moment will disappear. Instead, it becomes more detailed.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P058: “Maybe because you aren't thinking about how to explain it to someone else.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P059: The sentence could have become the start of a philosophical conversation, and Alice almost prepared to defend herself. But Eric suddenly added:
paragraphs.S66.C000.P060: “Or because Nick with a towel is hard to forget.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P061: “Thank you. You saved both of us.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P064: He turned toward her. Less than a step remained between them. Alice felt warmth from the open door and cold from the railing at her back.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P066: “I do. That's why I try not to draw them on the fourth day.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P069: “I was hoping to learn who I'd become in the article.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P070: “So far, you're a man who steals chocolate buns and pretends it's strategy.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P072: “Do you want to sit up front tomorrow?” Eric asked. “For the first hour of the drive.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P073: “I'll see in the morning,” Alice answered. She liked that he asked instead of silently leaving the seat for her.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P074: Nick came out of the kitchen.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P075: “Am I interrupting?” he asked, with the expression of someone who very much hoped he was.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P077: Nick put a hand over his heart.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P078: “At last, the group has learned to speak plainly.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P079: He held out a mug to Alice.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P080: “Tea. Damir said you take sugar now. I didn't believe him, so I put the packet separately.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P081: Alice took the mug. Damir stayed in the kitchen, not looking out to see what choice she would make.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P083: “I'm in charge of the music for the first forty minutes tomorrow,” Nick said. “The plan is approved.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P085: “On the condition that the yellow hat comes too.”
paragraphs.S66.C000.P088: Nick took the yellow hat from his pocket. Alice noticed that Eric was no longer looking at his phone. She had not answered his invitation yet, but she had not looked away either.
paragraphs.S66.C000.P089: Alice took a sip of tea. The sugar sat beside it, not added in advance. She tore open the packet and poured in half.

S66.C001.title: If Alice offered Damir coffee in S08-C1

paragraphs.S66.C001.P000: In the kitchen, she noticed that Damir had set out two clean mugs, the same ones they had drunk coffee from that morning. He caught her eye; they smiled at each other without continuing the conversation.

S66.C002.title: If Alice kept her distance in S08-C1

paragraphs.S66.C002.P000: She left the rest of the sugar beside the mug and did not go into the kitchen, where Damir remained. He did not come out to see what she had decided. Alice felt calm at the simple possibility of not continuing the morning's conversation.

S66.C003.title: If Alice asked about Brussels in S08-C1

paragraphs.S66.C003.P000: Damir stepped out of the kitchen for a minute and showed her one photograph: three bicycles and three friends outside a wet brick house. Alice remembered asking about it that morning and let her gaze rest on people she had not known before. He did not tell a story about each of them; she only asked which one had taught him to ride in the rain.

paragraphs.S66.C004.P000: In her room, Alice placed the saved ace between the pages of her notebook. Beside the notes about the greenhouse, she added three observations without trying to turn them into conclusions about people.
paragraphs.S66.C004.P001: Her phone vibrated. Marina had sent a single question: “Do you have a first paragraph?”

S66.C005.title: If Alice chose people in S02-C1

paragraphs.S66.C005.P000: Alice reread the paragraph: “In the greenhouse, we transplanted seedlings for a group we would never meet. Nick mixed up the tags; Eric quietly brought a new tray, and Damir held the pot while I looked for the right name. I remembered not the faces, but who kept working once it was clear that no one was filming us.”

S66.C006.title: If Alice chose place in S02-C1

paragraphs.S66.C006.P000: Alice reread the paragraph: “In Hveragerði, the rain drove us under the glass of a greenhouse. Warm water ran beneath the rows of tomatoes; lamps burned above them although it was still daytime outside. We came in to wait out the weather and stayed to help with seedlings for the next day's tour.”

S66.C007.title: If Alice chose her own decision in S02-C1

paragraphs.S66.C007.P000: Alice reread the paragraph: “We could have waited out the rain at a table, but stayed to transplant seedlings for the children coming the next day. Nick left the camera in his bag; I put away the notebook. For an hour, no one had a reason to look more interesting than they were.”

paragraphs.S66.C008.P000: She sent the paragraph to Marina. Marina replied almost at once: “Keep it. What happens tomorrow at the waterfall?” Alice did not know yet, but for the first time she wanted to find out for more than the article.
paragraphs.S66.C008.P001: A door closed quietly in the hallway. From the footsteps, Alice could not tell who had passed: Eric moved almost silently, Damir always stepped down heel first, and Nick might suddenly decide to sneak for the sake of a joke. A folded sheet appeared under the door a second later.
paragraphs.S66.C008.P002: Nick had drawn a yellow hat on it; Eric—probably Eric—had written the departure time beside it. Below, Damir had left a short note: “Don't forget your scarf.”
paragraphs.S66.C008.P003: Alice pinned the sheet to a page in her notebook.
paragraphs.S66.C008.P004: Voices sounded in the hallway. Nick suggested looking for the most unexpected place from which to see the waterfall tomorrow, rather than the best shot. Eric answered that he would show them the trail if the weather allowed. Damir asked whether they could simply get there and look around first. Alice opened the door.
paragraphs.S66.C008.P005: “I'm coming with you,” she said. “And we'll choose the place together.”
paragraphs.S66.C008.P006: Alice did not close the door: the conversation about tomorrow's place continued with her there.
